questions.q: What is the core claim of 'Attention Is All You Need'?
options: RNNs should always be combined with convolutional layers
A strong sequence-to-sequence model can be built using attention alone, with no recurrence or convolution
Positional encoding is unnecessary for sequence models
LSTMs outperform all other architectures for translation
questions.explain: The paper's titular thesis is that self-attention and cross-attention alone, without any recurrent or convolutional layers, can build a competitive sequence-to-sequence model.

questions.q: In the Transformer's decoder layer, what three sublayers are stacked, in order?
options: Convolution, pooling, feed-forward
Masked self-attention, cross-attention over the encoder output, feed-forward
Self-attention, recurrence, softmax
Positional encoding, self-attention, recurrence
questions.explain: Each decoder layer runs masked self-attention, then cross-attention over the encoder's output, then a feed-forward sublayer, each wrapped in a residual connection and layer norm.

questions.q: What role does cross-attention play specifically within the Transformer's decoder?
options: It lets the decoder attend over the full encoder output while generating the target sequence
It replaces the need for token embeddings
It is only used during training, never at inference
It computes the final loss function
questions.explain: Cross-attention in the decoder uses the decoder's own hidden states as queries and the encoder's output as keys and values, letting the decoder look back at the source sequence.

questions.q: Why were multi-head attention and positional encoding both necessary additions in this paper's architecture?
options: They are not actually necessary -- the paper works without them
Multi-head attention restores representational variety and positional encoding restores a sense of order, both of which recurrence had provided implicitly in earlier architectures
They were added only to reduce the parameter count
They are only used in the encoder, never the decoder
questions.explain: Removing recurrence meant losing both its implicit variety (addressed by multiple attention heads) and its implicit order (addressed by positional encoding), so the paper needed both additions.

questions.q: Why is 'Attention Is All You Need' considered the ancestor of most modern large language models?
options: Because it was the first paper to use neural networks for any task
Because its parallelizable, attention-only design scaled well with data and compute, leading directly to encoder-only, decoder-only, and encoder-decoder descendants like BERT and GPT
Because it eliminated the need for GPUs entirely
Because it was published by the team that later built every major LLM
questions.explain: The Transformer's attention-based, parallelizable design turned out to scale remarkably well, and its core building blocks underlie essentially all major modern LLM architectures.
